title: Cluster sidecar — morning scratch & action list
content:
Quick morning scratchpad — sidecars + capacity + networking

Top-of-mind today (short):
- reclaim candidate nodes from pool 'inference-burst-3' (older kernels, OOM sidecar traces). mark for drain after 14:00 UTC.
- verify sidecar memory leak metric (sidecar.heap_growth) across eu-west-1 nodes — spike around 02:00 in last 3 days.
- nvlink flakiness: node r7-23 shows degraded link on 2 GPUs (alerts from prom: nvlink_errors_inc). schedule hardware check? open ticket to colo ops if persists.
- check autoscale policy for Dedicated pool A: burst cap still set at 16, need confirm with billing before bumping.

Immediate TODO (ordered):
1) grep journal on r7-23 for nvlink logs: sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -o short-iso --since "2026-03-12 00:00" | grep -i nvlink -> copy to ticket.
2) run memory snapshot on sidecar for pod inference-serve-221: curl localhost:9100/heap | gzip -9 > /tmp/sidecar-heap-221-$(date +%s).gz
3) add canary route to runtime PR 7123 for canary subset (5 pods) before merging. mark rollout window 03/14 09:00-11:00 UTC.
4) notify @sre-team in #prod-builds: we might need eBPF flowcheck if packet drops rise after drain.

Notes / Observations (raw):
- last night drain on pool 'inference-burst-2' left 2 pods in Pending for >20m — something to do with CNI attach timeout (aws eni throttling?). file INFRA-891 reference.
- sidecar heap growth correlates with long-tail reqs (>1.5s tail latency). hypothesis: unbounded buffer for streaming websocket sessions.
- temporary mitigation: reduce sidecar max-stream-buffer to 8MB in canary. test on 5 pods.

Questions to answer / followups:
- Can we bump Dedicated burst capacity from 16 -> 20 for a 24h window for the demo? Who signs? @platform-ops or finance?
- Are there kernel versions in r7 batch that require immediate reprovisioning? list nodes and kernel versions.
- If nvlink hardware is flaky, do we move workload to software-only quantized model variant (v2-q4_0) during reprovision?

Slack / ticket breadcrumbs:
- INFRA-891 (linked) — CNI/ENI attach flakiness after draining pool inference-burst-2.
- PR: runtime#7123 — sidecar buffer fixes + tracing headers. need canary.
- Slack: #sre-team, #infra-ops, thread: "drain fallout 03/12".

Commands/snippets I keep repeating:
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=300
- kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide --selector=app=sidecar | grep Pending
- prometheus query for heap: avg_over_time(sidecar_heap_bytes{job="sidecar"}[3d]) by (node)

Checklist before end of day:
- [ ] nvlink logs captured and attached to ticket (r7-23)
- [ ] canary updated with max-stream-buffer=8MB, 5 pods
- [ ] autoscale bump request drafted and sent to billing
- [ ] drain test review with SRE (confirm ENI headroom)
- [ ] brief note to product (demo owners) if we plan burst bump

Notes to self (random):
- if canary shows improvement, roll to eu-west-1 pool at 30% traffic for 2h.
- instrument an extra histogram for websocket duration (sidecar): sidecar_ws_duration_seconds_bucket.

End scratch — will update after nvlink grep + snapshot runs.

Small log of edits:
- 2026-03-11 09:12 created skeleton while on morning run
- 2026-03-13 08:37 added nvlink notes after overnight alert
- 2026-03-13 09:04 blocked until canary config reviewed by Leah
